: 
The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 15.03.2023 at about 12.30 p.m. Venkatarayappa was walking on extreme left side of the road near Chigatenahalli Village Curve, Chigatenahalli, Chikkaballapura, a tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA40A 7088 came in high speed, rash and negligently and dashed against him, due to the impact, he fell down and sustained multiple injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Government District Hospital Chikkablalapura, thereafter shifted to Victoria Hospital Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient, underwent surgery and amputation of left leg SCCH5 and left hand, he was in ICU for 3 days and succumbed to the fatal injuries on 02.06.2023 and post mortem was conducted at Government District Hospital Chikkaballapura.
Petitioner No.1 is his wife, petitioner No.2 is his brother, they have spent an amount of Rs.20,000/ towards transportation of dead body and Rs.1,00,000/ towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
3. At the time of the accident, deceased was aged about 67 years, agriculturist and doing poultry farm, thereby earning Rs.36,000/ p.m.

Out of the said accident, crime No.27/2023 is registered Venkatarayappa vs Muniraju.P on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176478970/
2 before the Nandi Giridhama Police for the offences punishable under Sec..279, 337 of IPC agaisnt the driver of the said tipper lorry.
R1 is R.C.Owner, R2 is insurer of the tipper lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay SCCH5 compensation.

Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.80,00,000/.
4.
On service of notice, R1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

R2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying case of the petitioners, admitted issuance of insurance policy to the tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA40A7088 and liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act, further submitted that, said tipper lorry is not at all involved in this accident, the driver of the tipper lorry was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, said lorry was not holding valid permit to ply in the place of accident, claim made by the SCCH5 petitioners is higher side, hence his petition is not maintainable.

5. On going through the pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether petitioners prove that, on 15.03.2023 at about 12.30 p.m. when petitioner was walking on left side near Chigatenahalli Village Gate, at that time, one tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA40A7088 drivenb its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom ?

3. What order or award?
6.
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1(b) has deposed his evidence as PW1, examined one witness SCCH5 as PW2 and marked 16 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed her evidence.
On the other hand, R2 has deposed his evidence as RW1 and marked 4 documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4 and closed his evidence.
7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
Venkatarayappa vs Muniraju.P on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176478970/
3  ::REASONS::
8.
Issue No.1:
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1(b)/brother of the deceased has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chiefexamination he has SCCH5 reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar with sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of P.M. Report is marked as Ex.P.8, copy of inquest with statement of witnesses is marked as Ex.P.9, copy of additional complaint is marked as Ex.P.10, copy of requisition give to court is marked as Ex.P.11.
9 . There is no crossexamination denying place, date and time of the accident, further there is no dispute in written statement about place, date and time of the accident, further suggested that,
petitioner No.1(b) is not dependent of the deceased, said suggestion is denied.
SCCH5 Further admits that, he is not eyewitness to this incident, further denied that, he has not made any expenses.
10. PW2 is Medical Record Technician at Victoria Hospital furnished authorization letter, MLC Extract and case sheet which are marked at Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.16.

In crossexamination deposed that,
he do not know anything about treatment and documents.

11. On the other hand, R2/insurer has deposed his evidence as RW1 and furnished authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1, copy of policy is marked as Ex.R.2, copy of permit is marked as Ex.R.3, copy of letter issued to insured to produce the documents is marked as Ex.R.4 by stating that tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA40 A7088 not caused this accident, driver of the lorry had no driving licence and permit.

Further there is no negligency of the driver of the said lorry, insurance SCCH5 policy,
permit and also copy of letter issued against the owner to produce the documents.
In cross examination admits that, very accident is occurred on 15.03.2023 and permit is ended on 12.03.2023.
Further denied that, R1 moved an application before the RTO for renewal of the permit prior to 15 days of the date of expiry of the permit.
Further admits that, Investigation Officer has not filed charge sheet alleging that, there was no permit at the time of accident.

12. On perusal of the police papers it is noticed that, charge sheet is only for the offences punishable under Sec.279, and 304(A) of IPC R/w Sec.134 of IMV Act, but not stated anything as such there is no permit.

In crossexamination of RW1, counsel for petitioner herself posed a question that,
permit is ended on 12.03.2023 and this accident is occurred on 15.03.2023, SCCH5 her defence is that, owner has moved application before the RTO prior to the accident for renewal of the permit,
but she has not furnished copy of such application, even she has not made efforts to secure the owner of the vehicle and examine before this court.
Under such circumstances, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, there was no permit as on date of the accident.

Further this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, there was no application for reneweal of the permit prior to the accident, as per the contention taken by the petitioner, hence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, as on the Venkatarayappa vs Muniraju.P on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176478970/
4 date of accident there was no permit.
13.

It is defence of the R2 that, driver of the tipper lorry by name Narayaswamy K.N. had no driving licence at the time of accident, but to prove the said facts he has not furnished any evidence, except his oral evidence.
SCCH5 Further there is no charge sheet to that extent.
Under such circumstances, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, counsel for R2 has taken vague defence about the driving licence.
Further comes to the conclusion that, as on the date of accident, driver of the tipper lorry had effective driving licence.
14. Further it is defence of the R2 that, this tipper lorry has not caused this accident, but to prove the said facts, except his oral evidence there is no document on the side of the R2.

On the other hand,
Ex.P.1 to Ex.

P.7 i.e., FIR to charge sheet speaks that, very tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA40A 7088 has caused this accident, this accident is occurred on 15.03.2023, complaint is lodged on the very day, on the very tipper lorry.
Considering these aspects, this tribunal comes to the SCCH5 conclusion that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the tipper lorry.

15. Further it is noticed that, very accident is occurred on 15.03.2023, immediately on 21.03.2023 this petition is filed by the counsel for the petitioners for the relief of compensation, but unfortunately very petitioner is died on 02.06.2023 in the home of petitioner No.1(b).

Accordingly further requisition of petitioner No.1(b) before police as per Ex.P.10, accordingly further requisition is given before the Magistrate as per Ex.P.11 to include Sec.304(a) of IPC, inquest is conducted as per Ex.P.9, post mortem is conducted as per Ex.P.8.
On going through the same it reveals that, out of the very accident, death is caused, said fact is not disputed by the R2.
R1/owner has not at all contested the petition.
SCCH5 Considering all these aspects, I have answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:

As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Venkatarayappa was aged about 67 years as on the date of accident, for proof of age of the deceased, petitioners have produced copy of aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.12, wherein year of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 1956, the alleged accident was occurred in the year 2023.

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.12 age of the deceased is considered about 67 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 5 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as agriculturist and also doing poultry SCCH5 farming, thereby earning Rs.36,000/ p.m. to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.
Hence considering the same, this court relied upon the Karnataka Minimum Wages for the year 202223.
In the case on hand, petitioner is doing agriculture work and poultry farming, so that, he comes under category of formerly group - IV - now unskilled.

Very accident is occurred on 15.03.2023, accordingly unskilled workers minimum wages including dearness allowance comes to Rs.13,821/, so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of Venkatarayappa vs Muniraju.

5 dependency.
18.

Further petitioner No.1(a) is wife, petitioner No.1(b) is brother of the deceased Venkatarayappa,
to prove the said facts, they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar cards marked as Ex.P.12, it reveals that, they SCCH5 are the legal representatives of the deceased, hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

19. Counsel for the petitioner argued that, petitioner No.1(a) is wife of the deceased, they have no issues, petitioner No.1(b) is real brother of the deceased, petitioner No.1(b) has taken care of the deceased.
Further he has performed the funeral ceremony and obsequies ceremony of the deceased.
Further petitioner No.1(b) has borne medical expenses, so that, he was also dependent on the deceased.

Hence prays to consider his dependency and allot compensation for him along with petitioner No.1(a).
20.

On the other hand, counsel for R2 argued that, petitioner No.1(a) is wife of the deceased so that,
she is only entitled for compensation.
Further argued that, petitioner No.1(b) might have performed funeral and SCCH5 obsequies ceremony of the deceased.
Further he might have borne medical expenses, but he will not become dependent of the deceased.
So that, he is not entitled for compensation.

21. In support of his defence, he has relied upon a judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Anand Pal and others in Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (Civil) No.7805/2022 dated 04.12.2023 wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that,
'married brothers of the deceased will not become dependents of the deceased, only wife and children of the deceased will become dependents of the deceased, they are entitled for the compensation.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Anand Pal and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even it is observed that, if father is having independent income, he will not become dependent of the unmarried son, with such observation SCCH5 compensation is granted only for mother of the deceased and not granted compensation in favour of the brother of the deceased'.
22. In the case on hand, there is no pleading and proof by the petitioner No.1(b) to show that, he was depending on the income of the deceased.

Further he has not proved that, what kind of loss caused to him due to death of the deceased, at the most he might have incurred expenses for medical, for funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses, if it is borne by him, but which can be recovered from the petitioner No.1(a) after receipt of the compensation by her in this case.

Further it is noticed that,
petitioner No.1(a) and her husband were resident of Kanivenarayanapura, Muddenahalli,
Chikkablalapura District.
Petitioner No.1(b) is resident of 1st Main, 1st Cross, behind Sampangirami Reddy Angadi, SCCH5 Kaveri Nagar, Bengaluru North.
Furthermore available evidence speaks that, petitioner No.1(b) is living with his wife and children separately.
Furthermore deceased was married and separate with his family in some other place.
Under such circumstances, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner No.1(b) will not become dependent on the earnings of the deceased, however he has lost his real brother.
Under such circumstances, at the most he is entitled for loss of filial consortium of Rs.40,000/.

So that, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner No.1(a) is entitled for compensation and petitioner No.1(b) is not entitled for any compensation except loss of filial consortium of Rs.40,000/.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if there is sole dependent, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted SCCH5 towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/2 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

24. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, there is no addition to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged above 60 years.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,24,600/
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
29.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.0731023122P109335127 which is valid for the period from 17.12.2022 to 16.12.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 15.03.2023.
Further driver of the offending tipper lorry by name Narayanaswamy K.N. had valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
SCCH5 30.

As per the discussion made and findings given on the above issue No.1 tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA 40A7088 had no permit as on the date of accident, very fact is admitted by the counsel for the petitioner.

In this regard counsel for R2 relied upon judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.967/2017(MVD), dated 22.04.2022 in between Sri.Venkatesh V/s. IFFCO TOKIO General Insurance Co., wherein transport vehicle had no permit at the time of accident, so that, liability is fastened on the owner and appeal filed by the owner is dismissed.

31. On the other hand, counsel for petitioner relied upon a judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in 2023 ACJ 1952 in between G.Shivaputhra V/s. P.Shanthamma and others,
wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at para 6, 7, 15, 20 observed that, where there is no permit to the particular auto while plying on the road and not proved about filing of the SCCH5 application for renewal of the permit, under such circumstances, owner is liable to pay compensation, but considering the Sec.149(2)(a)(i)(a) of M.V.Act 1988 issued directions against Insurance Company to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner holding that, he has issued the insurance policy and which is in force at the time of accident.

Further relied upon a judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in between A.Banu Prakash V/s. Thimma Setty in MFA No.4945/2014 (MV) dated 01.09.2022 wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka passed order for pay and recovery relying on case of Pappu and others V/s. Yellavva and another reported in 2020 ACJ 2560 (HCK).

In the case on hand, insurance policy issued by the R2 is in force as on the date of accident.
Furthermore very accident is occurred only after 3 days of the expiry of the permit.
Under such circumstances it goes to show that, owner had no breathing time to get renew the permit.

So that,
this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just SCCH5 and necessary to pass the order for pay by the insurance company then recover from the owner.

33. Hence it is just and necessary to issue directions against R2/Insurance Company to satisfy the petitioners by way of depositing the award amount within 60 days from the date of this order with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and recover from the R1/owner through process of law.
Accordingly, I have answered above Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
34. Issue No.3:

Inview of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
SCCH5 The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,24,600/ (Rupees Five Lakhs Twenty Four Thousand Six Hundred Only).
Out of which, petitioner No.1(a) is entitled for Rs.4,84,600/ and petitioner No.1(b) is entitled for Rs.40,000/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order and recover from the respondent No.1 with due process of law.

The Petitioner No.1(a) is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The Petitioner No.1(b) is entitled to get release entire award amount through e payment directly to SCCH5 his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

3. At the time of the accident, deceased was aged about 67 years, agriculturist and doing poultry farm, thereby earning Rs.36,000/ p.m.
R1 is R.C.Owner, R2 is insurer of the tipper lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay SCCH5 compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.80,00,000/.
4.
R2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying case of the petitioners, admitted issuance of insurance policy to the tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA40A7088 and liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act, further submitted that, said tipper lorry is not at all involved in this accident, the driver of the tipper lorry was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, said lorry was not holding valid permit to ply in the place of accident, claim made by the SCCH5 petitioners is higher side, hence his petition is not maintainable.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On going through the pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether petitioners prove that, on 15.03.2023 at about 12.30 p.m. when petitioner was walking on left side near Chigatenahalli Village Gate, at that time, one tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA40A7088 drivenb its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom ?
3. What order or award?
6.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
12. On perusal of the police papers it is noticed that, charge sheet is only for the offences punishable under Sec.279, and 304(A) of IPC R/w Sec.134 of IMV Act, but not stated anything as such there is no permit.
Under such circumstances, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, there was no permit as on date of the accident.
Accordingly relying on Ex.P.12 age of the deceased is considered about 67 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 5 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.
In the case on hand, petitioner is doing agriculture work and poultry farming, so that, he comes under category of formerly group - IV - now unskilled.
Under such circumstances, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner No.1(b) will not become dependent on the earnings of the deceased, however he has lost his real brother.
Under such circumstances, at the most he is entitled for loss of filial consortium of Rs.40,000/.
So that, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner No.1(a) is entitled for compensation and petitioner No.1(b) is not entitled for any compensation except loss of filial consortium of Rs.40,000/.
Venkatarayappa vs Muniraju.
In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.0731023122P109335127 which is valid for the period from 17.12.2022 to 16.12.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 15.03.2023.
Further relied upon a judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in between A.Banu Prakash V/s. Thimma Setty in MFA No.4945/2014 (MV) dated 01.09.2022 wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka passed order for pay and recovery relying on case of Pappu and others V/s. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208 and also in the case in between New India Assurance Company V/s.
Yellavva and another reported in 2020 ACJ 2560 (HCK).
Further relied upon judgment of SCCH5 Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Challa Upendra Rao and others reported in (2004) 8 SCC 517, wherein relying on Sec.149(2)(a)(i)(a) of M.V.Act 1988 passed order for pay and recovery.
In the case on hand, insurance policy issued by the R2 is in force as on the date of accident.
Under such circumstances it goes to show that, owner had no breathing time to get renew the permit.
So that,
this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just SCCH5 and necessary to pass the order for pay by the insurance company then recover from the owner.
33. Hence it is just and necessary to issue directions against R2/Insurance Company to satisfy the petitioners by way of depositing the award amount within 60 days from the date of this order with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and recover from the R1/owner through process of law.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
21. In support of his defence, he has relied upon a judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Anand Pal and others in Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (Civil) No.7805/2022 dated 04.12.2023 wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that,
'married brothers of the deceased will not become dependents of the deceased, only wife and children of the deceased will become dependents of the deceased, they are entitled for the compensation.

Inview of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER
: : 
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
SCCH5 The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,24,600/ (Rupees Five Lakhs Twenty Four Thousand Six Hundred Only).
Out of which, petitioner No.1(a) is entitled for Rs.4,84,600/ and petitioner No.1(b) is entitled for Rs.40,000/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order and recover from the respondent No.1 with due process of law.
The Petitioner No.1(a) is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The Petitioner No.1(b) is entitled to get release entire award amount through e payment directly to SCCH5 his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
